species.real: Hops are in the same plant family as cannabis. English ale was long brewed without them; hopped 'beer' came over from the Low Countries in the 1400s.
species.name: Hoplet

dex.text: Climbs anything that stands still long enough, always clockwise. Smells pleasantly of a pub garden in September.
dex.fact: Hop bines climb clockwise round their strings. Every September thousands of Londoners came down to Kent for hop-picking, a working holiday in the hop gardens.

species.real: Kent's round oasts, called roundels, were built in the belief that round kilns heat more evenly; builders later went back to square ones because they were easier to build.
species.name: Oastcowl

dex.text: Its white cowl swings round to keep its back to the wind, and its insides stay at a steady drying heat. Excellent company on a cold night.
dex.fact: An oast house dries freshly picked hops over a kiln. The white cowl on top turns with the wind to draw the warm air through; most oasts are now homes.
